- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3%.
- If sentiment spikes (≥0.53) followed by a sharp price rise, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- When model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising values) with low sentiment, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops after a peak), model often fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average and sentiment is neutral or negative, apply downward correction to avoid “over-leveraged” bias.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, assume model is “overfitting” to recent volatility; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.53 → 0.18 → 0.53), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average to smooth forecast.
